questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go abroad to challenge myself personally and academically and experience a different study environment. I also wanted to expand my network. I primarily chose Uppsala because I wanted to study in a city that was smaller than Copenhagen and because the Swedish education system is very similar to the Danish.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: What I recall when thinking of my stay in Uppsala are the people I've met and spent most of my time with. The academic level at SLU was lower than what I had expected, which was quite disappointing. However, I was fond of the relationship between students and professors especially when I was writing my thesis. I felt very respected.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The introductory program was quite extensive. Maybe a bit too much -  a lot of repetition all the time. There were some days with online lessons, which I think was quite unnecessary.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was easy to get to know what I wanted to know. Also all international students were included in the introduction program for Swedish students  - regarding social activities. And it was possible to participate the amount you felt like. All activities was quite cult-like though... Which I didn't like.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I found it though SLU. It was easy. 
At first i tried to find a house to rent with some friends, but it was impossible.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a must to live off campus I would say. SLU is quite far from the town center, and I guess you would take less advantage of the city if you lived on campus. Cute houses on the SLU campus though

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very lucky to stay with some people of whom I already knew a few. It was nice that that was taken into account when the rooms were distributed.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit inconvenient that you had to sign up for courses on a separate web side than the one from the university.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite smooth as I remember it. However it was hard to get an overview of the courses. And if you were not attentive you could risk registering for two courses running in the same period.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write the exchange coordinators at SLU if you had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to get admitted to the classes I wanted. I also managed to change the course I originally had signed up for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware in which period a course is running before registering.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level and the work load of the courses I attended were lower than expected.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The content of the courses was a bit superficial considering that it was masters level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It really depended on the course. Some were very interactive, and some were not at all. But all in all the style of teaching was quite similar to that of UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Introduction to Environmental Communication
2. Models for Sustainable water management
3. Geographic information systems for environmental and natural science studies

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Master thesis in Environmental science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend Introduction to Environmental communication to students who are interested in social sciences but have a natural science background. It gives a really good introduction to how to understand and work with people in environmental management. 
I would not recommend the GIS course. It hadn't been updated since 2020. They are also teaching an outdated version of the GIS software.

Bike repairs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transport
Food especially fresh vegetables

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Most of the activities that were promoted at SLU were party and drinking oriented. Which a lot of people really like. I think I might just have become an old, boring master student..
However there were also other sports and outdoor activities which was really nice

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Different sports and outdoor activities. I don't really know. A lot of parties too. 
They also offered a language café where you could learn Swedish. 
The association for international students also planned different activities in relation to the Swedish national holidays.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: None, they all kind of sucked

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend to get out into the woods whenever its possible. There are also a lot of public huts in national parks in the area. 
Stockholm also has a lot of really nice museums which are worth a visit.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: As I am Danish it was not too difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The student nations are good places for socializing. And also the long lunch breaks at SLU.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found the alcohol culture quite un-charming..

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The right of public access, making it easy to get into the wild.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: That its worth it. And that they do not have to love every moment. And that they should take advantage of the surroundings. Winter is even longer in Sweden than in Denmark, but its worth the wait because spring is really, really beautiful.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can not get a beer in town if you are not a member of a student nation. Get yourself used to standing in line - Swedish people really like it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think is was most rewarding for my personal development. I did meet amazing people who made a great impression on them. And now I know I have people spread out all over Europe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To leave my relations from home. And to get used to a new university.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: 10/10 can recommend.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
